units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 44">Gen. R. s. 44</cite> <he>ש׳ השם</he> change of name; <he>ש׳ מקום</he> change of residence.
<cite ref="Shabbat 114a:1">Sabb. 114ᵃ</cite> top <he>ש׳ בגדים</he> change of dress (for the Sabbath, for prayer &c.).

Keth. 110ᵇ, a. e. ש׳ וסת, v. וֶסֶת; a. fr.—Esp. (law) change of form (and name) effected on an illegitimately obtained object, by which the present possessor is privileged to retain the object and pay its value.
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 65b:12">B. Kam. 65ᵇ</cite> <he>נעשה ש׳ בידו וקנאו</he> the change (from calf to ox) happened while the animal was in his possession, and he has obtained ownership.

<cite ref="Bava Kamma 65b:19">Ib.</cite> <he>וניקנינהו בש׳ השם</he> may he not have obtained the ownership of it through the change of name? <cite ref="Bava Kamma 65b:19">Ib.</cite> <he>ש׳ במקומו עומד</he> (not <he>עומדת</he>) the change stands in its (the original’s) place, i.e. the change of form or name of an object does not affect its legal status; <cite ref="Bava Kamma 93b:17">ib. 93ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Bava Kamma 68a:16">ib. 68ᵃ</cite> <he>ש׳ במקומה עומד</he>.
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 66b:6">Ib. 66ᵇ</cite> <he>ש׳ מעשה</he> (= <he>ש׳ ע״י מעשה</he>) a change brought about by human action.
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 68a:16">Ib. 68ᵃ</cite>, a. fr. <he>ש׳ רשות</he> change of possession (by transfer of the object to a third person).

<cite ref="Bava Kamma 93b:6">Ib. 93ᵇ</cite> <he>ש׳ דרבנן</he> a change which gives the right of ownership by rabbinical ordinance, i.e. <he>ש׳ החוזר לברייתו</he> (<cite ref="Bava Kamma 67a:8">ib. 67ᵃ</cite>) a change (of name) which can be undone by restoring the object to its original condition; <he>ש׳ דאורייתא</he> a change which gives the right of ownership by Biblical law, i.e. a change which cannot be undone; a. fr.—

<cite ref="Menachot 43a:2">Men. 43ᵃ</cite> <he>וסימנך ש׳ שקר ש׳ אמת</he> and the mnemonical word (to remember which change proves the color to be genuine (<cite ref="V00547"><he>תכלת</he></cite>), and which proves it to be adulterated) is ‘a false change’ (one who changes his word for evil is a bad man), ‘a true change’ (one who changes his word to do better than he has promised).—Sifra Vayikra, Ḥob., ch. XIX, Par. 11; <cite ref="Meilah 18a:34">Meïl. 18ᵃ</cite>, v. <cite ref="U01047"><he>שִׁיקּוּר</he> I</cite>.—Pl. <he>שִׁינּוּיִים</he>, <he>שִׁינּוּיִין</he>.

<cite ref="Bava Kamma 65b:19">B. Kam. 65ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="C00993"><he>גם</he></cite>, <cite ref="Deuteronomy 23:19">Deut. XXIII, 19</cite>) <he>לרבות שִׁינּוּיֵיהֶם</he> this serves to include in the prohibition these objects even when they have been changed in form; <cite ref="Temurah 30b:45">Tem. 30ᵇ</cite>; a. e.
